dashboard.label: Help & Dependencies
dashboard.definition:
{
  "title": "KO History: Help & Dependencies",
  "description": "How the wrapper, the ko_version_ds dashboard, the index, the saved searches and the custom visualizations depend on each other.",
  "dataSources": {},
  "inputs": {},
  "visualizations": {
    "viz_md_overview": {
      "type": "splunk.markdown",
      "options": {
        "markdown": "# KO History: how the pieces fit together

**KO History** captures and versions Splunk knowledge objects into a summary
index so you can audit changes and recover content after accidental deletes,
overwrites, or moves. Seven types are covered: dashboards, reports and alerts,
search macros, event types, field extractions, lookup definitions, and tags.

This page is a map of the app's moving parts and, importantly, **what depends on
what**. Read it before renaming a view, moving the index, or changing the
dashboard's selection markers.

| Piece | Type | Role |
|---|---|---|
| `ko_home` | Dashboard Studio | The landing page and app default. Pure Studio on purpose: it resolves without a restart, unlike the Mako-templated React pages. |
| `wrapper` | React app page (Mako) | The main page. Embeds `ko_version_ds`, drives preview / compare / **restore**. |
| `ko_version_ds` | Dashboard Studio | The actual data UI: filters, KPIs, KO table, version list, textual diff, **source viewer**. |
| `ko_version` | Simple XML | Legacy/alternate dashboard, labelled **KO Version (SXML)** in the nav to tell it apart from the Studio one; SXML live-render preview via `dashboard_preview`. |
| `ko_settings` | React app page | Admin settings. Enables and disables the capture searches, restore per object type, and the index name. |
| `index=ko_history` | summary index | Append-only version log. Everything reads from here, via the `ko_history_index` macro. |
| saved searches | 15 stanzas | Populate the index (7 type backups + combined delete-audit + 7 one-time backfills). |
| custom viz `source_viewer` | bundled viz | Foldable, syntax-highlighted KO source. Used in `ko_version_ds` **and** (its logic) in the wrapper. |
| custom viz `dashboard_preview` | bundled viz | Live dashboard render for Simple XML host (write-then-iframe). |
| custom viz `ko_viewer` | bundled viz | Splunk-native record card for one KO version (reports/alerts get a bespoke profile). |
| `ko_help` | Dashboard Studio | This page. |
"
      }
    },
    "viz_md_capture": {
      "type": "splunk.markdown",
      "options": {
        "markdown": "## What actually gets captured

Two different kinds of event land in `index=ko_history`, and the difference
matters when you are reading the version list.

**Backup snapshots** (`ko_*_backup`, one per type) hit the REST API on a
staggered 15-minute cron and write one event per KO that changed. The event
carries the object's full source or configuration, so it is what a restore
replays. Crucially, `_time` is set to the KO's own `updated` timestamp, **not**
the time the search ran. That is what turns the index into an append-only
version log rather than a log of collection runs.

**Audit records** (`ko_all_delete_audit`, hourly) scrape splunkd access logs in
`_internal` for DELETE and POST move against KO REST URIs. They carry no source,
because by then the object is gone. They are the only place the acting user is
recorded, which is what lets the dashboard answer "who deleted this".

| Type | Backup search | REST endpoint behind it |
|---|---|---|
| Dashboards | `ko_views_xml_backup` | `data/ui/views` |
| Reports & alerts | `ko_reports_and_alerts_backup` | `saved/searches` |
| Search macros | `ko_macros_backup` | `admin/macros` |
| Event types | `ko_eventtypes_backup` | `saved/eventtypes` |
| Field extractions | `ko_fieldextractions_backup` | `data/props/extractions` |
| Lookup definitions | `ko_lookups_backup` | `data/transforms/lookups` |
| Tags | `ko_tags_backup` | `configs/conf-tags` |

**Only changes are captured.** Each backup ends with a `where updated>now`
filter scoped to the `ko_backup_window` macro (default 900 seconds). Widening
that window without widening the cron interval re-indexes the same version on
every run. The wrapper's scratch preview slots are excluded by name, so
previewing never pollutes the history.
"
      }
    },
    "viz_img_capture": {
      "type": "splunk.image",
      "options": {
        "src": "/static/app/ko_history/images/capture-flow.svg",
        "preserveAspectRatio": true
      }
    },
    "viz_img_dependency": {
      "type": "splunk.image",
      "options": {
        "src": "/static/app/ko_history/images/dependency-map.svg",
        "preserveAspectRatio": true
      }
    },
    "viz_md_dependency": {
      "type": "splunk.markdown",
      "options": {
        "markdown": "## Dependency map

- **The index name lives in one macro.** Every search in the app reads it as
  ``index=`ko_history_index` ``, and the macro expands to the bare index name
  (`ko_history` by default). Change the macro and every dashboard and lookup
  builder follows. It is the supported way to point the app at an index you
  already have, or to run under a name your naming policy requires.
- **Changing it needs the write side too.** The macro governs where the app
  READS. Where it WRITES is `action.summary_index._name` on each capture search,
  which is a saved-search setting and cannot use a macro. Change the macro alone
  and the dashboards look at the new index while capture keeps filling the old
  one: a working install showing an empty table. Use **Settings**, which updates
  both together. Editing the macro directly on *Settings > Advanced search >
  Search macros* is supported, but then you must repoint the capture searches
  yourself.
- **Saved-search `source` values are the discriminator.** The `koType` dropdown
  uses `ko_views_xml_backup`, `ko_reports_and_alerts_backup` (the per-type backup
  searches) and the combined `ko_all_delete_audit` (which replaced the former
  per-type `ko_views_delete_audit` / `ko_reports_and_alerts_delete_audit` sources).
  Renaming a saved search means updating every `source IN (…)` clause.
"
      }
    },
    "viz_md_contract": {
      "type": "splunk.markdown",
      "options": {
        "markdown": "## The wrapper ↔ ko_version_ds contract (read this before editing either)

The React **wrapper** does not re-implement the data UI. It **embeds
`ko_version_ds` in a same-origin iframe** and communicates with it through two
one-way channels. Break either channel and the wrapper goes inert.

**1. Selection flows dashboard to wrapper via two marker panels.**
`ko_version_ds` carries two markdown panels for this:

> `viz_link_label` (human, display only):
> `Selected: <title> · app: <app> · type: <type> · older: <time>`
>
> `viz_link` (machine, read by the wrapper, **invisible**: it is rendered with a
> transparent font colour, so it is present in the DOM but not on screen):
> `kohist-sel: <title> ⟪|⟫ <app> ⟪|⟫ <ko_class> ⟪|⟫ <epoch>`

A real example, taken from clicking a lookup called `kodemo_lookup` in the
`search` app before choosing a version:

```
kohist-sel: kodemo_lookup ⟪|⟫ search ⟪|⟫ lookup ⟪|⟫
```

**The four fields**

| Field | Token | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| title | `$link_title$` | The object's name. May contain spaces and punctuation. |
| app | `$link_app$` | The app the object lives in. |
| ko_class | `$ko_class$` | One of `dashboard`, `savedsearch`, `macro`, `eventtype`, `fieldextraction`, `lookup`, `tag`. Decides which panes the wrapper offers. |
| epoch | `$time$` | Integer seconds of the **older** version selected in the version list. **Empty until a version is clicked**, as in the example above. |

**Why the delimiter is `⟪|⟫`.** A plain `|` would collide with SPL and with
knowledge-object names. The sequence has to be something that cannot occur in
real content, because the fields are positional and unlabelled.

**Two states that are not errors and must not be treated as selections.**
Before anything is clicked, `link_title` and `link_app` hold a placeholder dash,
and unresolved tokens arrive literally as `$link_title$`. The wrapper rejects
both, otherwise it would try to load version history for an object named after
the placeholder. Both dash glyphs are accepted: the generator emits an en dash,
but a dashboard generated before that change emits an em dash.

**The empty epoch is the normal case, not an edge case.** The KO table's
drilldown sets title, app and class but not `time`; only the version list sets
`time`. So the *first* click on any object always produces a marker ending in a
delimiter with nothing after it. A parser that requires a value there drops
every first selection, which is indistinguishable from the app being broken.

**How the wrapper reads it.** On a **click** inside the embedded dashboard, with
a few delayed re-reads because Dashboard Studio updates tokens asynchronously,
plus a 5-second heartbeat that also re-attaches the click listener after an
iframe reload. Reading is done through `textContent`, which never triggers
layout. A last-resort full-body scan exists for builds where no targeted
selector matches, rate-limited so it cannot become a hot loop.

**If you change any of this**, the wrapper stops detecting selections: deleting
the `viz_link` panel, renaming `link_title` / `link_app` / `ko_class` / `time`,
or altering the `kohist-sel:` prefix or the delimiter. The parser and its tests
live in `src/util/markerParse.js` and `tools/dev/test_marker_parse.js`; change
the format in the generator and that test tells you what broke.

**2. Preview / compare / restore flow wrapper → Splunk via REST.**
The wrapper writes dashboard source into **scratch "slot" views** in *this* app
and then iframes them:

- `kohist_cmp_baseline_<user>`, `kohist_cmp_target_<user>`: the compare modal's two render slots (suffixed with the sanitized current username since 0.1.93; falls back to unsuffixed when unavailable).
- Restore writes a **real** view into the app you pick (default = origin).

This needs **write access to `data/ui/views` in `ko_history`** for the viewing
user. `metadata/default.meta` grants write to `admin, sc_admin`. **Do not broaden
the `[views]` write stanza**. The vizs export as `system`, so that grant becomes a
view create/overwrite primitive reachable from any dashboard, gated only by a
client-side prompt. The browser approval prompt is convenience, **not** security.
Splunk RBAC is the real gate.

**3. The app id must stay `ko_history` (underscore).** The React Mako page cannot
live under a hyphenated app id. Renaming the app breaks `PREVIEW_APP` /
`KO_INDEX` and the iframe URLs.
"
      }
    },
    "viz_img_marker": {
      "type": "splunk.image",
      "options": {
        "src": "/static/app/ko_history/images/marker-protocol.svg",
        "preserveAspectRatio": true
      }
    },
    "viz_md_react": {
      "type": "splunk.markdown",
      "options": {
        "markdown": "## The React wrapper page: what it is & how it points at the dashboard

The home page `wrapper` is **not** a dashboard. It's a Splunk **Mako template +
webpack-bundled React app** (`@splunk/react-page`), served at
`/app/ko_history/wrapper`. Source lives in `ko_history/src/` (entry
`pages/wrapper/index.jsx` → `components/WrapperApp.jsx`); `build.sh` compiles it
to `appserver/static/pages/wrapper.js`. It runs with the **user's real session**
(cookies + CSRF), which is the whole reason it can do authenticated REST and
same-origin iframes that a sandboxed DS custom viz cannot.

### How it references `ko_version_ds`

It **embeds the dashboard in a same-origin `<iframe>`**. The URL is built in
`WrapperApp.jsx` (the `dashUrl` memo):

```
/<locale>/app/ko_history/ko_version_ds
    ?hideEdit=true&hideTitle=true&hideChrome=true
    &hideSplunkBar=true&hideAppBar=true&hideFooter=true
```

- `<locale>` is read from the current page URL (e.g. `en-US`, `en-GB`), not hardcoded.
- The app segment comes from the constant **`PREVIEW_APP` (`ko_history`)** in
  `src/util/splunkRest.js`.
- The **view id `ko_version_ds` is a string literal** in `dashUrl`.
- The `hide*` query params strip all Splunk chrome so only the dashboard body shows.

### Can the reference be changed / updated?

Yes, but it is a **compile-time constant in the bundle, not a runtime setting**.
There is no setup screen and no `.conf` knob for it. To change it:

| To change… | Edit | Then |
|---|---|---|
| Which dashboard is embedded | the `ko_version_ds` literal in `dashUrl` (`WrapperApp.jsx`) | `./build.sh` + reinstall + **full restart** |
| Which app it lives in | `PREVIEW_APP` in `src/util/splunkRest.js` (also moves slots/REST target, only when renaming the whole app) | `./build.sh` + reinstall + **full restart** |
| What chrome is hidden | the `chrome` string in `dashUrl` (and `previewUrl`) | rebuild |

Because the embed target is baked into `wrapper.js`, **editing the dashboard XML
on disk and reloading is not enough for wrapper changes**. The static bundle
needs a rebuild and a full `splunk restart` (a reload won't refresh it).

### The authenticated REST endpoints the wrapper calls

All same-origin, under `/<locale>/splunkd/__raw/servicesNS/nobody/<app>/…`, with
the `splunkweb_csrf_token` cookie echoed as `X-Splunk-Form-Key`:

- **Read versions / list apps**: `search/jobs` oneshot against `index=ko_history`.
- **Compare**: POST `eai:data` to scratch slot views `kohist_cmp_baseline_<user>` /
  `kohist_cmp_target_<user>` in `ko_history`, then iframe them (chrome-stripped, cache-busted).
  Slot names are suffixed with the sanitized current username (since 0.1.93) so
  concurrent compares by different users don't overwrite each other's slots.
- **Restore**: POST `eai:data` to `data/ui/views/<name>` in the **app you choose**
  (writes a real dashboard; 403 = you lack write on that app).

So the wrapper depends on `ko_version_ds` for the *embedded UI + selection
signal*, and on the *index + its own write access* for compare/restore. These
are two independent dependencies, documented above and in the contract section.

"
      }
    },
    "viz_md_rest": {
      "type": "splunk.markdown",
      "options": {
        "markdown": "## The dashboard REST API: two layers (and why KO History exists)

Splunk exposes dashboards through two distinct REST layers. The distinction is
the whole basis for this app.

### Layer 1: `…/data/ui/views` (BOTH formats)
`servicesNS/{owner}/{app}/data/ui/views` is **format-agnostic**: every view is a
row, whether it's Dashboard Studio (`<dashboard version="2">`) or Classic Simple
XML (`<dashboard>` / `<form>`). Create / read / update / delete all behave the
same; the format lives in the `eai:data` envelope. Verified live on a Splunk
10.4 instance: a single call returned **261 views = 153 DS + 108 Simple XML**.
**KO History uses this endpoint** for snapshot backups, the compare preview
slots, and one-click restore, which is exactly why it works for both formats.

### Layer 2: `…/data/ui/views/{name}/history` & `/revision` (Dashboard Studio only)
Native dashboard **version history** is a Dashboard Studio feature (Splunk 10.x).
Its REST surface applies **only to Studio dashboards**, captures a version **only
on explicit save**, stores history **with** the dashboard (delete it → history is
gone), and is gated (single search head; not on FIPS-mode Windows). Simple XML
has no native revisions. Evidence: the standard view entry advertises links
`_reload / alternate / edit / list / disable / move / remove`, with **no `history` or
`revision` link**, so it's a separate, DS-only surface.

### The gap KO History fills
Full CRUD exists for both formats, but **native versioning covers only DS, only
on save, stored with the object.** KO History versions **Simple XML too** (plus
reports/alerts) via periodic snapshots into `index=ko_history` that **survive
deletion** and **restore to any app**.

"
      }
    },
    "viz_img_rest": {
      "type": "splunk.image",
      "options": {
        "src": "/static/app/ko_history/images/rest-layers.svg",
        "preserveAspectRatio": true
      }
    },
    "viz_md_viz": {
      "type": "splunk.markdown",
      "options": {
        "markdown": "## Custom visualizations & the DS sandbox

Dashboard Studio runs every custom visualization in a **sandboxed iframe**, so no
cookies, no authenticated fetch, no child iframes. That single fact shapes the
whole design:

- **`source_viewer`**: pure client-side formatting of a source string. Sandbox-safe,
  so it runs natively inside `ko_version_ds` (the *Source of selected version*
  panel) and its logic is reused client-side in the wrapper's **Source** compare
  tab. Reads columns `data` / `title` / `app`.
- **`dashboard_preview`** (SXML): live render via write-then-iframe; only works
  in Simple XML, where same-origin iframes are allowed.
- **`ko_viewer`**: record-card viz for saved searches and generic KOs (macros,
  event types, field extractions, lookups, tags) with field-level diff; DOM-based,
  sandbox-safe.
- **The wrapper exists** precisely because it is *not* sandboxed: as a real app
  page it has the user's session, so it can do authenticated REST and same-origin
  iframes (live preview, restore) that a DS custom viz never could.

All three vizs are `export = system` in `metadata/default.meta` so they appear in
the viz picker. The viz type is `<app>.<viz>` → e.g. `ko_history.source_viewer`.
"
      }
    },
    "viz_md_operating": {
      "type": "splunk.markdown",
      "options": {
        "markdown": "## Operating it

### 1. The index must exist first

Nothing works until `ko_history` exists. `default/indexes.conf` ships with the
app and sets a 20-year frozen period, which is the setting that stops old-dated
snapshots being aged out. That file applies **only on a search head**:

- **Splunk Enterprise, single search head:** a full restart picks it up. Nothing
  to do.
- **Splunk Enterprise, indexer cluster:** create `ko_history` through your
  cluster manager before enabling anything.
- **Splunk Cloud:** create an Events index named `ko_history` via the Admin
  Console. The bundled `indexes.conf` is inert there.

### 2. Enable the capture searches

**Every search ships `disabled = 1`.** This is deliberate: an app that starts
writing to a non-existent index on install is worse than one that waits. Enable
the seven `ko_*_backup` searches and `ko_all_delete_audit`. The quickest route
is this app's own **Settings** page, which lists every shipped search grouped by
what it does with a switch on each; Splunk's Settings, then Searches, reports and
alerts, works too. Wait one cron cycle, roughly 15 minutes.

### 3. Seed history for objects nobody has touched (optional)

The incremental backups only capture a KO once it is *edited*. An object that is
never touched after install and then deleted would have no snapshot to restore
from. The seven `ko_*_backfill` searches close that gap: they snapshot every
current object of their type, writing to the same summary source as the matching
backup so the dashboards see them transparently.

Run each **once, manually**, then leave it disabled. There is no dedup, so
re-running duplicates snapshots. Each backfill also ships a commented-out
`| collect` line for the case where you paste the SPL into a search bar, where
the saved search's summary-index action does not apply.

"
      }
    },
    "viz_md_restore": {
      "type": "splunk.markdown",
      "options": {
        "markdown": "## Restore: what it does, and what it does not

Restore writes a **real knowledge object** into whichever app you pick, from the
snapshot you selected. It is the reason the app exists, so it is worth being
precise about its edges.

**What you get back:** the object's source or configuration exactly as captured.
For a dashboard that is the full XML or Studio JSON. For a saved search it is
the search string, schedule, alert condition and trigger actions.

**Restore ships switched off.** It is the only thing this app does that writes
back into your environment, so nothing is restorable until an admin turns it on,
per object type, on the **Settings** page in the app nav. Enabling it writes
`local/ko_history.conf`, which is also the only route on Splunk Cloud, where the
filesystem is not reachable. Capture, version history, preview and compare are
unaffected and work with everything switched off.

If you upgraded from 1.1.x, this is a change: restore used to be on for
dashboards and saved searches. Turn it back on from the Settings page.

**Which types can be restored.** All seven types are captured, previewed and
compared. One-click restore covers **dashboards and saved searches**. Restore
for macros, event types, field extractions, lookups and tags is implemented but
has not finished testing, so the settings page lists them as greyed-out
placeholders. Setting those keys to `1` by hand does nothing: the app intersects
what you enabled with what has actually shipped. Their history is still
captured, so nothing is lost while it is switched off.

**A greyed-out Restore button always says why.** Hover it. There are three
different reasons, and they are not interchangeable: the type is disabled in
settings, the type has not shipped yet, or the settings could not be read at
all. The last one fails closed on purpose.

**What you do not get back:**

- **Sharing and ownership.** Restored objects are written as owner `nobody`
  (app-shared). The original ACLs are not replayed. Re-apply permissions
  yourself if they mattered.
- **Lookup file contents.** A lookup's *definition* is versioned; the underlying
  `.csv` or KV-store collection is not, and is not restored.
- **Tag removals.** Restoring tags re-enables the captured assignments on a
  `field=value` pair. Tags added since the snapshot are not removed.

**Restoring over an existing object is irreversible** and requires a separate,
explicit confirmation in the UI. If KO History also has a snapshot of what you
overwrote, that snapshot is your way back. If it does not, there is none.

**You need write access** to `data/ui/views` (or the relevant endpoint) in the
target app. Restore is an admin capability by design; see Permissions below.
"
      }
    },
    "viz_md_history": {
      "type": "splunk.markdown",
      "options": {
        "markdown": "## Reading the version list

A few behaviours surprise people the first time.

- **The oldest snapshot is labelled "created".** It is the earliest record the
  app holds, which is not necessarily when the object was created: anything
  before the capture searches were enabled is simply not there. Backfill events
  carry the object's own edit time, exactly like the incremental capture, so
  seeding the index does not flatten your history to one date.
  Backfill events also carry `backfill=1`, so you can always tell a seeded
  snapshot from one observed live.
- **A knowledge object that has never been edited has no timestamp at all.**
  Splunk's REST API reports epoch 0 for one, which renders as 1970 in UTC and as
  1969 anywhere west of it, and `strptime` returns null for that value rather
  than 0. The capture searches therefore parse the timestamp first and then test
  the resulting epoch, which is the only form of the test that works in every
  timezone. The format string matters just as much: it carries no literal `+`
  before `%:z`, because a `+` there matches only a positive UTC offset and would
  make every object on a search head west of UTC look like it had no timestamp.
- **What those objects are dated, and why it differs by search.** The
  incremental capture maps them to a fixed **2010-01-01**. That is an exclusion
  sentinel, not a guess: its job is to be older than the capture window so the
  `where updated>now` clause drops the row, which is what stops a never-edited
  object being re-captured every fifteen minutes forever. It has to be fixed
  rather than relative, or the same object would be stamped differently on every
  run, and it has to stay inside `frozenTimePeriodInSecs` (20 years as shipped),
  which means 2010 stops being safe around 2030.

  The backfill searches keep the value instead of discarding it, so a constant
  there would be a visible falsehood: every undated object in your
  environment sharing one meaningless date. They date it **one second past the
  start of the year of the oldest edit that run could see**. The claim is only
  "at least as old as anything else here", which is the strongest true statement
  available for an object carrying no timestamp, and the odd `:01` second is the
  marker that says the date was manufactured rather than read. If nothing in the
  run has a usable timestamp at all, they fall back to the time the search ran.
- **Delete and move rows have no source.** They come from the audit stream, so
  they cannot be previewed, diffed or restored. They tell you *what happened*
  and *who did it*, not *what it looked like*.
- **The version list is capped at the 200 most recent** entries per object. A KO
  edited hundreds of times will not show its whole history in the picker.
- **Preview runs the dashboard's real searches.** A snapshot preview is a live
  render, so a heavy dashboard costs what it normally costs. The cost flag on
  the panel warns before you commit, and calls out unbounded time ranges, which
  are usually the expensive part.
- **Comparing writes two scratch views**, `kohist_cmp_baseline_<user>` and
  `kohist_cmp_target_<user>`, inside this app. Your real objects are never
  touched, and the slots are per-user so two admins do not collide.
"
      }
    },
    "viz_img_pairing": {
      "type": "splunk.image",
      "options": {
        "src": "/static/app/ko_history/images/version-pairing.svg",
        "preserveAspectRatio": true
      }
    },
    "viz_md_permissions": {
      "type": "splunk.markdown",
      "options": {
        "markdown": "## Permissions (read before granting anything)

`metadata/default.meta` grants read to all roles and write to `admin` and
`sc_admin`. **Do not broaden the `[views]` write stanza.**

The reason is specific, not cautious boilerplate. All bundled visualizations
export as `system`, so they are usable from dashboards in any app. Any role
granted `[views]` write **in this app** therefore gains a view create-and-
overwrite primitive that is reachable from any dashboard, fleet-wide. The
browser approval prompt in the wrapper is a convenience, not a security control:
it runs client-side and cannot be relied on as a gate.

If non-admin roles genuinely need preview or restore, the supported path is a
constrained server-side endpoint (a custom REST handler enforcing per-user and
per-slot limits), not a wider write grant.

**The settings page follows the same rule.** `ko_history.conf` is readable by
everyone, because the wrapper has to know whether restore is enabled before it
can draw the button, and writable by `admin` and `sc_admin` only. The page
decides whether to show you controls or a read-only view by asking the endpoint
whether *you* can write that stanza, so it stays correct if you change the
permissions rather than depending on a hardcoded role name.

Being explicit about the limits of that: these settings are a policy control,
not a security boundary. Anyone who can restore through KO History can already
create or overwrite the same objects through Splunk's own UI. What the settings
give you is a deliberate switch and a default of off, so nobody restores
something by reflex on an instance where that was never intended.
"
      }
    },
    "viz_md_troubleshooting": {
      "type": "splunk.markdown",
      "options": {
        "markdown": "## Troubleshooting

**The KO table is empty.** The index exists but nothing has been captured yet.
Confirm the searches are enabled and that at least one cron cycle has passed.
``index=`ko_history_index` | stats count by source`` tells you whether events
are arriving and from which search.

**A dashboard I know exists has no versions.** The backups only capture objects
that change. Until someone edits it, or you run the matching backfill, there is
nothing to show.

**Versions load slowly, or time out.** The wrapper bounds a version search at 30
seconds and then offers Retry. A consistently slow search usually means a very
large index with a wide time range; the searches deliberately run over all time
because backfilled events can carry old timestamps.

**Opening KO History or Settings returns a server error.** Almost always a
missing restart, and it is the single most common thing to go wrong on a fresh
install. The symptom is a 5xx error page, usually a 500, sometimes with a stack
trace ending in

```
TopLevelLookupException: failed to locate the template for uri
'ko_history:/templates/wrapper.html'
```

Both pages are React pages served from a Mako template plus a static bundle, and
Splunk resolves both when the appserver **starts**, so before a restart they
cannot be found. Nothing prompts you to restart, on Splunk Cloud or on
Enterprise. Restart Splunk and open the page again. Every other page in the app,
including this one, works without the restart, so a working nav and a broken
main page is exactly the expected shape of this problem.

**The wrapper page looks stale after an upgrade.** Same cause, different symptom:
the bundle Splunk resolved at startup is the previous version's. Copying files or
reloading the app is not enough, and a stale bundle is more confusing than a
missing one because the page loads and merely behaves oddly. A **full
`splunk restart`** is required after every upgrade, not just the first install.

**Preview boxes do not appear.** The in-iframe highlighter tries a ladder of
selectors and may need tuning on an unusual Splunk build. The structural change
list and the source diff never depend on the iframe DOM, so they still work.
"
      }
    },
    "viz_md_install": {
      "type": "splunk.markdown",
      "options": {
        "markdown": "## Install & rebuild notes

- **Deploy = tarball only.** `./build.sh` at the repo root builds the custom-viz
  bundles + the React page and packages `dist/ko_history-<version>.tar.gz`.
  Install that tarball; do **not** hand-edit files inside a running Splunk.
- **Full restart for the React bundle.** Changes to the wrapper's static bundle
  need a full `splunk restart` (a reload is not enough) plus a hard browser
  refresh.
- **Regenerate dashboards** after editing their generators:
  `python3 tools/gen_ko_version_ds.py` and `python3 tools/gen_ko_help.py`.
- **This page** is generated by `tools/gen_ko_help.py`: edit the markdown there,
  not the committed XML.
"
      }
    },
    "viz_md_changes": {
      "type": "splunk.markdown",
      "options": {
        "markdown": "## Notable changes

**1.1.0**

- The REST API Explorer and KO Statistics dashboards were removed. They were
  development tools rather than product surfaces.
- Searches now run as asynchronous jobs and are polled, replacing a blocking
  call that could leave the preview panel loading indefinitely on a slow
  instance.
- Every shipped search carries inline SPL comments.
- Apache-2.0 `LICENSE` ships with the app.

**1.0.3**

- `json_viewer` was renamed to `source_viewer`, and `dashboard_preview_ds` was
  removed. If you reference `ko_history.json_viewer` or
  `ko_history.dashboard_preview_ds` from your own dashboards, update them.
"
